chapter: Paris scene and a visit home, 1937-39
title: Germans at the hotel, the Rhineland and deciding to go home in 1938
summary: Butler noticed German guests and an English hanger-on, musicians being called up when Germany marched into the Rhineland, and in 1938 decided to visit his family in New York.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Now, there were a lot of, in the meantime, people coming there with knickerbockers on, pants, you know, Germans They were coming in and visiting in my hotel. The man was named Josef. He was the clerk and he was the man who would take care of everything. Josef used to speak in German and all this stuff. I didn't pay it no mind.
Then there was quite a few Englishmen, they

were hanging around our band all the time. One man was named Peter. Peter was hanging around all the time. And we noticed that people were talking. See, the Germans had marched into the Rhineland and a couple of musicians, they had to put on their uniforms and go to the Rhineland, because they, they had to go to the Rhineland.
After the Germans come out of the Rhineland, everything seemed to be all right. Everybody was calm. There were rumors, he is going to start a war.
Now, we are coming down to 1938, 1938 and I said, I believe I'll go home and see my people, so I went. I come to New York.
